articles.title: CoreWeave Revenue Jumps 168% as Results Revive AI Trade and Lift Nasdaq
articles.excerpt: The AI cloud company's $3.66 billion quarter beat expectations, its backlog reached $132.5 billion, and its shares rose 24.7% — even as its net loss widened to $709 million.

articles.title: Goldman Sachs Adds a March Rate Hike to Its Federal Reserve Forecast
articles.excerpt: Goldman Sachs now expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates by 25 basis points in March, abandoning its call that the hiking cycle would end in December, after October inflation came in hotter than expected for a third straight month, Reuters reported.
articles.nri_angle: Goldman's higher-for-longer path affects diaspora households directly through US mortgage and borrowing costs, with no cut in its forecast until December 2027.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.nri_angle: Diaspora investors in Indian equities saw a broad post-Diwali intraday rally driven by FII buying, cheaper crude and a stronger rupee, with levels stated as live snapshots.

articles.title: Gold Falls Sharply in Dollars, but Indian Gold ETFs Still Hold Gains Since Last Diwali

articles.title: Bitcoin Slides Toward $73,000 as Hot CPI Revives Fed Rate-Hike Bets
articles.excerpt: October inflation rose 0.4 percent, above the 0.3 percent forecast, and core prices also beat expectations. Bitcoin fell to about $73,400 after the print, Treasury yields jumped, and traders now price a December Fed hike as near-certain, with a small chance of a half-point move.
articles.nri_angle: Higher-for-longer US rates flow through to mortgage, remittance and portfolio decisions for Indian households in the US; bitcoin's drop is part of a broader risk-asset repricing, not a crypto-specific event.

articles.title: HSBC and Citi Turn Bullish on India as Foreign Inflows Head for a Record Week
articles.excerpt: HSBC upgraded India to overweight and Citi raised its end-2027 Nifty target to 28,000 after overseas funds bought $3.6 billion of shares in four days.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI investors holding India exposure through funds or direct equities, the practical read is that foreign positioning in India was light — the upgrades argue flows, not just valuations, now support the market.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: KOSPI Closes 4.39 Percent Higher as Samsung, SK Hynix Lead Chip Rebound

articles.image_caption: KOSPI
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora investors tracking Asian chip exposure, the KOSPI's 4.39% close higher was a dip-buying rebound whose next test is U.S. inflation data.

articles.title: PepsiCo to Cut About 1,000 North America Jobs in Restructuring
articles.excerpt: North America CEO Ram Krishnan told staff the changes, due within a week, will simplify a structure he called complex and fragmented, after beverage volumes fell 2% last quarter.
articles.image_caption: Pepsi bottles are pictured on a store shelf. PepsiCo is cutting about 1,000 jobs across North America as it restructures after a weak third quarter in its home market.
articles.nri_angle: PepsiCo's North America chief Ram Krishnan, who announced the restructuring, is one of the most senior Indian-origin executives in US consumer goods; the cuts affect a workforce with a large South Asian presence.

articles.title: India's Festive Season Split Its Scoreboard: Trade Up, Household Spending Down
articles.excerpt: Traders forecast a record Rs 7 lakh crore season while a 67,000-household survey found planned spending down 6% — the distance between the two is the story of Diwali 2026.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs holding Indian consumption and retail stocks, the split festive data — strong trade volumes, cautious households — is the signal to read before earnings season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Rally Defies Global Rout, but Analysts Warn the Rotation Can Reverse
articles.excerpt: Benchmarks are up about 10.5 per cent in seven sessions while the S&P 500 posted its worst week since April 2025. Strategists call it a rotation out of AI stocks, not a decoupling — and say it holds only while the selling stays in technology.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora investors holding both US tech and Indian equities, India's low AI-hardware weight is currently acting as the portfolio hedge — with named conditions that would end it.

articles.title: Gold Rebounds Above $4,100 Despite Strong US Payrolls, Ahead of Inflation Test
articles.excerpt: Spot gold traded at $4,121.77 on Monday after Friday's 165,000-job payrolls surprise knocked it toward $4,033 — Tuesday's US CPI print now decides whether the rebound holds, with December hike odds near 80%.
articles.image_caption: Gold crystals are shown in close-up. Spot gold reclaimed $4,100 on Monday after a stronger than expected US payrolls report knocked it toward $4,033 on Friday.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian households and NRI investors who bought gold through the festival season, the level to watch is $4,100: holding it into Tuesday's CPI keeps the festival-season rebound intact, losing it reopens the $4,000 test.

articles.title: Dalal Street Week Ahead: Inflation, Earnings and Foreign Flows Decide the Rally
articles.excerpt: After the Nifty reclaimed 25,000 on a Rs 45,960 crore foreign buying week, a holiday-shortened week brings India and US inflation prints, continuing Q2 earnings and a test of whether foreign flows hold.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI investors in Indian equities, the week tests whether the foreign inflow that powered the Diwali rally is a durable return or a one-week reversal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Selloff Is a Speed Adjustment, Not a Bust, iM Securities Says
articles.excerpt: Semiconductor stocks fell 11.4% in the days around the US midterms while hyperscaler shares rose, a split iM Securities says points to slower AI spending growth, not an end to the investment cycle.
articles.image_caption: The Korea Exchange in Busan is pictured in a Wikimedia Commons photograph. A Seoul-based iM Securities strategist called the global AI selloff a speed adjustment rather than a bust.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora investors holding US chip and AI names, the split between falling semiconductor shares and steady hyperscalers is the signal to watch before treating the selloff as a cycle end.

articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai. India's Nifty 50 gained 8.6 percent last week as foreign funds returned to local shares.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI investors concentrated in US AI names, the rotation is a live diversification question: India and China are drawing the flows their portfolios may be missing.

articles.excerpt: The fear gauge closed at 28.18 on November 5 as the S&P 500 fell 4.41% and the Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.5%. In Bespoke's 19 similar spikes since 1990, the S&P 500's median return six months later was 4.8%, positive 79% of the time — with a negative average over the first month.
articles.nri_angle: Many diaspora investors hold US index and semiconductor exposure through 401(k)s and brokerages; the Bespoke table gives them the sourced historical odds, and the limits of those odds, after the year's sharpest fear spike.
